newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to Oct 25.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) has reported a 3.1 percent rise in its turnover during the week ending October 25 and traders said the market was in a wait-and-see mood ahead of Yugoslav federal elections on Sunday.
Total weekly turnover on BSE stood at 23.545 million dinars ($4.68 million) in 156 transactions, compared to 22.83 million dinars in 165 deals a week ago, the bourse said on Monday.
"It was a feeble week. Lots of funds have been withdrawn on fear from a possible dinar devaluation after the elections," a trader told Reuters.
The fear stems from earlier experience and the fact that the dinar is artificially held stable, the trader said.
The BSE saw no trade in the central bank short-term bonds last week.
Most activity was based in the commercial paper segment with 129 transactions worth 18.257 million dinars.
Treasury bills were traded 20 times for a volume of 2.845 million dinars.
Interest rates both on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between an annual 331 and 644 percent.

Pre-polls slowdown in market activity did not by-pass the unofficial giro money market where banks trade their surplus liquidity. The volume on this market fell to 35.48 million dinars from 45.17 million a week ago.
"There is definitely enough money on offer, but not enough clients with good credit history. Funds are given only to those who can really pay back," a trader said.
The trader cited a powerful debtors' lobby as the biggest problem of the market. "They do not meet maturities and cannot pay the interest rate, no matter how low it may be."
It is easy to find a debtor, but very difficult to find an investor, another trader said.

"The volume of our market is very low. We talk about some 200-400 million dinars of funds available for investment. If someone could provide some 50 million dinars that would really move the market and set the terms, a trader said.
Traders agreed the financial market needed a stronger government commitment to privatisation. "Otherwise, we'll keep working in a very limited market with no long-term instrument to invest in."
Lack of such a commitment and uncertainty weigh on the only longer dated paper traded on the bourse.
The BSE reported four deals in wheat selling forward contracts, worth 2.043 million dinars.

Contracts were launched on October 3 and will be on sale until December 3. They were originally aimed at banks, flour mills and bakeries. But from next Monday, individuals will join a targeted group of investors.

The face value of the wheat selling contract is 9,000 dinars with 10 tonnes of wheat sold as collateral. The contract carries a 32 percent discount and matures July 15, 1997. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
